FFI vs bc2sa: Two Paths for Bringing in External Code

SA / SLA deal with the C/C++/Rust world along two paths of opposite direction:

  • FFI — the SA side declares @extern "C" functions and connects directly to native code via the ABI at runtime. The code does not enter the SA pipeline; it stays in the native .so/.dll.
  • bc2sa — external source is compiled into LLVM bitcode and then translated in as SA text; the code enters the SA pipeline and is managed by the same verification/release artifacts.

FFI: calling via the ABI at runtime

Sla directly supports exporting and calling C ABI functions. For a real example, see the rosetta demo demos/rosetta/111_extern_c_abi/main.sla:

@import "sa_std/io/print.sai"
@import "sa_std/fmt.sai"

@no_mangle pub extern "C" fn add_pair(a: i32, b: i32) -> i32 {
    a + b
}

fn main() -> i32 {
    let result = unsafe { add_pair(11, 12) };
    println("{}", result);
    return result;
};

Key points:

ItemDescription
Export@no_mangle pub extern "C" fn — the symbol is exported per the C ABI and can be called by the host or other native code
Call boundaryCalls across the ABI are wrapped in unsafe { … }, explicitly marking "the verifier cannot see the other side"
Data surfacesa_std/ffi.sal provides the CStr/CString layout constants (reusing the Slice trio) and the CSTR_*/CSTRING_* error codes, handling NUL termination and UTF-8 validation; ffi/cstring.sal and ffi/prelude.sal are submodule aggregations
MaturityA usable path: rosetta 111 has a full check/build/test chain comparison (a Rust reference main.rs + the Sla version main.sla)

bc2sa: translating bitcode into SA

sa bc2sa file.bc (see the bc2sa plugin page for details) takes the compile-time route: clang/rustc produce LLVM bitcode → it is translated into SA text → it enters the same downstream pipeline as handwritten SA. It currently covers only a conservative subset (no phi/switch/select/floating point/atomics); only O0 artifacts may pass.

Selection comparison table

DimensionFFIbc2sa
DirectionCross-ABI calls at runtime; the external code stays in a native libraryTranslates external code into SA source at compile time
DeliverablesA two-piece set: the SA artifact + the dynamic libraryA single SA artifact (the translated code is already merged in)
Safety verificationInside the unsafe boundary, the SA verifier cannot see the other side's behaviorThe translated instructions enter SA verification and the static rejection flow (GEP out-of-bounds reports StaticMemoryOverflow/SA-CLI-019)
Performance characteristicsOne ABI cost per FFI call; suits coarse-grained callsNo cross-language runtime overhead; on par with handwritten SA
DependenciesThe target platform's dynamic library + header-style contracts (.sai/signature declarations)The LLVM 14 toolchain (llvm-dis/as); on Windows there is also the child-process path problem
CoverageAny function conforming to the C ABIA conservative subset: unoptimized, integer, fixed GEP
Applicable scenariosCalling system APIs, ready-made third-party libraries, hardware bindingsA small amount of in-house C/Rust leaf-function source that must be included in SA verification/release
MaturityUsable (demo verified across the full chain)Experimental (the evaluation document's conclusion)
Rule of thumbUse FFI by default to connect ready-made libraries; only when the goal is "this piece of C/Rust source must become part of the SA artifact" should you consider bc2sa, and first confirm the code compiles at -O0 and contains no floating point/atomics/complex control flow.
